tasks.notes: Answers both halves directly - mutable tag versus artifact identity and cryptographic validity versus policy authority - and represents all five core claims, including fail-closed refusal when the digest cannot be re-resolved.

Fully explains hot-tenant skew and lists the resharding invariants (single owner, epochs, fencing, verification), but never addresses the core claim that mutable keys create move storms or that cross-shard work needs an explicit protocol.

Explicitly carries authorization, evidence and failure-mode reasoning for compensation and covers all core claims, though the alternative of one local transaction or two-phase commit is not mentioned.

States the processing-time state check, symmetric stale-event handling, total ordering by time/priority/insertion sequence and the worked timeout-before-completion sequence, covering all five core claims.
